observations: For Robin (requirement conflict): in V1, L3.1.3.1 (USB_MOUTH X in [-1.8, 0.5]) and L3.1.6.1 (Pico header pins on the board grid, residual <= 0.15) cannot both pass with the catalogue perfboard. USB_MOUTH X = first-pin X - 1.37 - 1.3, so the first pin would have to be at X 0.87-3.17, but the first grid column of the 80 x 60 board is at X 5.71 (and the catalogue's minimum grid margin is 4.74). A V1 design must therefore fail one of the two and can never MEET as written. The [-1.8, 0.5] window looks copied from the jack-mouth rule; something like [2.5, 3.5] (first pin on grid column 0, as E1-01's L2.1.3) would match the Pico. Graded as written.
Functionally the USB plug still seats with 0.40 mm clearance: its overmold enters the 10.8 x 7.8 opening and runs about 5 mm into the cavity over the board's -X margin, 1.4 mm above the board top.

The orange strips on the opening edges in model_left.png are OpenSCAD cut-face colouring, not geometry. No floating fragments, wrong-side walls or inverted lid seen.

The four lid-screw bosses stand outside the tray corners (OD 6.6, out to X/Y -6.59 and 86.59/66.59), which makes the convex hull larger than the tray; this does not open the cavity (sealed when the ports are filled).
